questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that it was a place with a different climate than i was used to, a new city i hadn't lived in or explored before and that it presented lots of opportunities for traveling and personal development throughtout the semester.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was great at sending all the information you needed before arrival and offered lots of assistance to those who need it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I personally didn't use any of the assistance offered as i have gone on exchange and lived abroad a couple of times before so i felt confident doing it on my own. I also didnt go directly to the city where my host university was located when arriving in Australia, and therefore lots of the help offered wasn't necessary or available to me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy to find affordable housing on my own. I teamed up with another student from KU when i got down there to look for housing. We looked for rooms via facebook and Flatmates (def recommend flatmates the most), and booked inspections for the next day. As they pay rent weekly it's very quick to find a place and move in within a week or a couple of weeks.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they should never pay any deposit or sign anything before having gone to a physical inspection. You need to be patient and wait until you arrive before looking as so many people get scammed, and as everything moves so quickly you can probably find something within a week. However i do reccommend that you explore the different areas and figure out where you are interested in living. Gold Coast is larger that you would expect and you could end up with a long commute. However finding a room somewhere near the tram line is what i recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A friend of mine lived in the UNI Village housing and was very dissatisfied. The area around campus is boring and far from the beach and the fun areas in town. Only upside is that its walkable to campus, however you will be living with a bunch of 17-year olds who has never lived on their own before. Several of the apartments also had major mold issues.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to have your preferred courses accepted by both the host institution and your home university. You enroll by searching for the coursecode and choosing your schedule as soon as enrollment opens in November (for trimester 1). If you find it confusing you can always wait and get help during O-Week, but you risk your classes being full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: During O-week theres several places to get help such as the library or the international student advisory lounge. Before you arrive, however, you can e-mail the school and they will guide you. As the professors has to accept you into their class, it can sometimes take a very long time before you know if your request are denied or accepted, but you just have to be patient.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I successfully registrered in almost all the classes i wanted. I had one class where i was denied due to not having met the prerequisites.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan your classes to be on the same days so you have long weekends every week to travel and explore. Also expect several assessments throughout the semester, whichcan seem stressful as they seem to require a bit of work, however, the expections and the quality actually expected seemed quite low and so you dont need to stress. You will be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one BA course and three MA courses. At BA level i felt the class and teacher were much more engaged and the level of education was decent, but quite low compared to what i expected. There was a good match between what was taught and what was expected in the assessments, however the teacher kinda carries everyone through it and seems to have very little faith in what you can do as an exchange student. My MA classes were all intensive and there was much reading before every class. However i found that the reading and the actual teaching didnt match up and neither did the assessments, so you had to do most of the work yourself. Class was also much less engaged and everyone very old. However i didnt find the level to be hard at all either, as you could skip the reading for classes and just focus on the required assessments.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, as all my lectures were online and then i had a workshop in person. At the workshops/tutorials on BA level they help you prepare for assessments. On MA level you only have lectures and so you can choose between watching online or in person when you want.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Media Law - BA
International Negotiations - MA
International Oragnisations - MA
International Environmental Law - MA

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Media law and International Organisations. I found both subjects interesting, and really liked how media law combined both a self chosen research topic on a current law reform and a case based assessment combining all the skills taught throught the class. In IO we were taught negotation skills and tricks and were placed in situations to these test out. Very different but fun.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt explore these much.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots but i didnt really participate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel travel travel all around Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as i have lived in Australia before, so i knew what to expect.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: How young people are in Uni and also that they all get up around 5am and go to bed around 20pm in the Gold Coast - also on weekends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How laid back they are

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Sorry, i really dont know.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a bit of a break and exploring someplace new. Also meeting a bunch of amazing people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably missing your friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
